In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuroendocrine system is affected in a complex manner in abstinent alcoholism, which is characterized by an impaired HPA response, but not a disturbed sympathetic activity.
the HPA and autonomic nervous system are not affected in a similar fashion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the autonomic and neuroendocrine responses of abstinent alcoholics to stress and i.v. CRFs differ from healthy subjects.
alcoholics have a blunted ACTH and cortisol response to CRF, but not to stress, and that the blunted ACTH release to CRF is not due to a blunted CRF release.
alcoholics are able to compensate for the blunted HPA response to CRF by increasing the secretion of other ACTH-releasing substances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hypothalamic and pituitary components of the HPA-axis are not necessarily affected to the same degree in alcoholics.
alcoholism is a disease that affects the entire body and that the effects are not just limited to the brain.
the CRF system may play an important role in the regulation of blood pressure in alcoholics.
